question:
A 31-year-old woman visits her physician with complaints of low energy and irritability lasting for
several weeks. She was thrilled after being accepted into a master's program, but after the semester
began, she started experiencing feelings of "worthlessness." Her history reveals self-reported "mood
swings," characterized by several weeks of increased productivity and elevated mood, followed by
several weeks of fatigue, guilt, and depressive symptoms. She is not on any medications and
consumes 2-3 glasses of wine on weekends. Physical examination findings are normal. Mental status
examination shows a tired-appearing woman with difficulty maintaining attention, requiring questions to
be repeated. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
(B) Persistent depressive disorder (C) Cyclothymic disorder (D) Generalized anxiety disorder (E)
Bipolar II disorder (F) Borderline personality disorder (G) Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (H)
Bipolar I disorder (I) Substance-induced mood disorder (J) Major depressive disorder
 A. Adjustment disorder with depressed mood
B. Bipolar I disorder
C. Borderline personality disorder
D. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
E. Bipolar II disorder
F. Cyclothymic disorder
G. Generalized anxiety disorder
H. Substance-induced mood disorder
I. Major depressive disorder
J. Persistent depressive disorder
